correctness.rationale: The four repeated intervals have explicit distinct occurrence witnesses; the non-obvious third equality is established inductively from k=2 by image boundary letters. The interval bridge lemma forces every unique factor to contain one of three bridges. Disjoint three-factor residue classes give exact occurrence synchronization of trimmed morphic images. The first bridge is uniquely a left-extended distinguishing prefix; the other two inherit uniqueness from base length nine. All three proper prefix/suffix factors are repeated. The symbolic induction proves all k>=2; suffix-array and independent brute checks pass at lengths 9-19683.

value.rationale: The exact MUS count and complete positions for every canonical Stewart choral iterate settle a natural word-identification statistic for a standard automatic/Toeplitz word. Unlike known critical exponent, cubefreeness or factor complexity, this requires new simultaneous repetition-cover and synchronization structure. It yields three linearly scaling anchors at exponentially growing sizes and is motivated by current work on MUSs of morphic words rather than a convenience parameter.
